newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Cash Converters to launch chain in Latin America.
newsitem.headline: Cash Converters to launch chain in Latin America.

text.p: Australia's Cash Converters International, a second-hand goods franchise chain, said it will soon open in Argentina the first of 80 stores it plans to install in South America over a five-year period.
"We believe we will be able to open by December our first store in Buenos Aires," Eduardo Averbuj, master franchisor for Cash Converters Sudamerica Ltd, told Reuters in an interview.
The company plans to open 60 shops in Argentina and a total of 20 more in Uruguay, Paraguay and Bolivia. It already has 400 stores in 27 countries around the world.
The 80 stores will mean an investment of about $20 million and the creation of hundreds of jobs. The chain will buy and sell second-hand jewels, electronics, and most portable goods.

"We met enormous success in Europe. The natural progression was to open stores in other communities with European culture," Cash Converters International chairman and founder Brian Cumins said. "It seems to me Argentina is even more European than the Europeans."
But he added the firm will also consider prospects in other Latin American countries like Brazil, Chile, Mexico and Venezuela.
Cummins said he expected a yearly average gross revenue of about $1 million per store.
